q-sop-04.Nothing more; a sounding horn is a pass: A sounding horn proves the horn and the power. Ask what else on the unit, besides the button, tells you about its condition.
q-sop-04.The expiry date printed on the battery: The horn already sounded, so power is fine. Ask what wears out in the alarm itself, not in the battery.
q-sop-04.Its smoke sensitivity, using a can of ae: Reread what NC asks you to do with smoke alarms: operate the test function. Ask whether spraying test smoke goes beyond that.

q-sop-32.Whether framing matches the construction: Plans show what was designed. Reread the exclusions at the end of .1117 and ask whether checking work against drawings is on that list.
q-sop-32.Wiring pulled for low-voltage and future: Reread the pre-drywall exclusions near the end of .1117. Ask what they say about preparation for future installations.
q-sop-32.Whether the framing is strong enough for: Ask whether a visual inspector calculates strength or design adequacy. Reread what .1117 says inspectors are not required to do.

q-ea-06.The panel's manufacture date and the rec: Brand recalls matter for some panels. Ask whether recall research is part of a visual inspection's required scope.
q-ea-06.Signs of a lightning strike or surge, an: Lightning damage usually shows as scorching, pitting, or melted parts. Ask whether the stem describes any of that.
q-ea-06.Moisture readings, with your meter press: Ask whether you press any tool against parts inside a live panel. Reread the course's dead-front safety rules.

q-er-13.Acceptable, because the cable is a flexi: Calling it a flexible cord renames the wire. Ask whether renaming it changes the installation rules that apply.
q-er-13.Not reportable; a disposal is an applian: Ask where the appliance exclusion idea came from. Reread the SOP's limitations and see whether a visible wiring connection is excluded.
q-er-13.Shock hazard; recommend replacing the di: Ask whether anything in the stem says the disposal or the circuit wiring has failed. Reread how the course sizes a recommendation.

q-ca-07.Not reportable; crawlspace ducts are out: Ask whether ductwork you can see in a crawlspace falls outside the HVAC part of the inspection.
q-ca-07.Cosmetic, as long as the insulation jack: Ask whether the stem's condition is about appearance at all. Reread how the course defines cosmetic, then weigh the rest.
q-ca-07.Duct system failure; recommend replacing: Ask how many joints the stem says have failed. Does one dropped run tell you about every duct in the house?

q-fp-04.Stage 1: Stage 1 is soft and sooty and brushes off. Ask whether a coating a scraper barely marks fits that.
q-fp-04.Stage 2: Stage 2 is crunchy and flaky and breaks apart under a tool. Ask whether that fits what the scraper did.
q-fp-04.Not creosote, just heat discoloration: Discoloration is a color change in the masonry itself. Ask whether a coating you can scrape at is just color.
